messages:
jules (AE): Quick ask 100k qps-month enterprise POC, peak ~5k RPS. They've signed MSA and want a firm reserved config + preheat/runbook and a simple pricing range for fp16 vs 4-bit quant. Also security Q: customer-managed KMS + 13mo logs.
ben (sales_eng): They emphasized a P99 token latency target of ~200ms and that ~40% of requests are chat sessions ~2k tokens. Also asked about model licensing for quantized variants.
sara (solutions): Suggested starting point: 6 reserved GPUs (A100-80 equiv) with burst credits to add +50% capacity (i.e., up to 9 GPUs). Split 3+3 across AZs for eviction tolerance. KV-cache warmup expected to reduce token compute ~25-35% for sessioned chat.
mark (infra): Ops items: autoscale rules and preheat recipe. Example autoscale: scale up if gpu_util > 70% for 30s -> +1 GPU; scale down if gpu_util < 30% for 5m -> -1 GPU. Burst policy: allow +50% for up to 4 hours/day via burst credits.
mark (infra): Preheat runbook (short):
- T-120m: start kv-warmup jobs across all reserved GPUs
- T-90m: run synthetic at 50% for 30m
- T-60m: run synthetic at 75% for 45m and validate p99
- T-0: allow burst credits for +50% capacity for initial ramp (4h)
mark (infra): Smoke commands: `./kv-warmup --model mix-quant --sessions 1200 --concurrency 120` and `./loadgen --rps 3750 --ctx 2000 --duration 45m`. Pass criteria: error rate <0.5% and p99 token latency <=200ms.
ops-bot: reservation-check OK, capacity available in region.
jules (AE): Pricing ask: please post a quick low/med/high range for 6-GPU baseline fp16 vs 4-bit quant so I can finalize the quote.
sara (solutions): Ballpark (example numbers): fp16 ~ "$72k/mo" for 6 GPUs. 4-bit quant + batching -> roughly 40-50% lower -> "$36k-$44k/mo". Burst credits billed at marginal premium (~+10%). Will send detailed calc.
jules (AE): Security: can Dedicated + customer-managed KMS + audit forwarding cover the 13mo logs requirement?
ben (sales_eng): Legal said Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and audit-forwarding satisfies that; Private only if they require air-gapped or on-prem. Add a model license clause if customer brings licensed quantized models.
jules (AE): They want contractual language about coldstarts. Can we do a conditional SLO?
ben (sales_eng): We can offer a conditional SLO: "P99 latency SLO of 200ms when the preheat runbook (KV warmup + synthetic smoke) is executed by customer/Redwood within agreed windows; otherwise best-effort." Legal to formalize.
sara (solutions): For rollout ops, recommend a canary ramp 10%->50%->100% on day one and an automatic fallback to a quantized (lower-latency) variant if thresholds breaching.
jules (AE): Next steps: Sara posts calc + sensitivity, Mark posts preheat checklist and synthetic smoke pass criteria, Ben drafts conditional SLO wording for legal. Need final AE deck numbers by EOD. Ping here when ready. :white_check_mark:
